title: Sharon Stone Reveals Premonition After Near-Fatal Stroke: 'Orbs Presented Themselves to Me'
excerpt: Sharon Stone spoke to Mayim Bialik about an apparition that came to her while she was recovering from her 2001 stroke.
content:
HEALTH

Sept. 8 2026, Published 12:36 p.m. ET

Sharon Stone opened up about a bizarre vision and premonition she had while she was recovering from her 2001 stroke, which was nearly fatal.

The Basic Instinct actress shared exactly what happened during a new conversation on Mayim Bialik's "Breakdown" podcast (via Entertainment Weekly).

Article continues below advertisement

Sharon Stone's Bizarre Vision

Stone explained that while her sleep patterns were disrupted, she had a sort of vision or apparition in her home.

"When I was first home from the hospital, I couldn’t sleep at night and I was sleeping in the day," she told the Big Bang Theory alum. "When I was laying on the couch, sleeping and awake, these orbs sort of presented themselves to me. These five orbs presented themselves to me and they sort of talked to me, but in a digital language."

Article continues below advertisement

Sharon Stone Had a Premonition About Her Son's Custody

While communicating with the orbs, Stone said that she cared above all about her son Roan, who was 1 years old at the time.

"I just kept saying to them, 'I don’t know if I’m supposed to stay here or if I’m supposed to die.' And they said, ‘You’re supposed to stay,'" she recalled. "And I said, 'I can only stay if two of you will stay with my son. Because I don’t want him to be alone, and I think he’s gonna get taken from me.'"

Unfortunately, she was right, and she lost custody of Roan to her then-husband Phil Bronstein when they separated.

"Sure enough, he was taken from me," she told Bialik. "And I said, 'We have to have an agreement. The two of you will stay with him and protect him.' And they agreed. And they said, 'But your destiny requires that we stay with you.'"

Sharon Stone's Near-Fatal Stroke

Stone unfortunately suffered a stroke in 2001, which dramatically impeded her career.

"People treated me in a way that was brutally unkind," she revealed in 2019 (via Variety). "From other women in my own business to the female judge who handled my custody case, I don’t think anyone grasps how dangerous a stroke is for women and what it takes to recover — it took me about seven years."
